_contract: Authored by Tasklet 2026-08-16 natively to contract v3, mirroring the Seattle v3 fleet-investors structure per the international addendum (UAE run — tourism-weighted utilization stack). Sources: dubai/REVENUE-STACK-DUBAI.md + CREW-COST-DUBAI.md + TOURISM-DEMAND-DUBAI.md + AUTHORITY-MAP-DUBAI.md + SPEED-RULES-DUBAI.md + GEOMETRY-DUBAI.json. CONTRACT v3: only `title` (<=6 words), `value`/figures, `note` (<=140 chars, partner-clean plain English), `status` (enum: market_priced | modeled | upside), and `fn` (footnote key) render — plus verbatim copy fields (headline/subline/body/chips/cards/quantity/price). Underscore-prefixed fields NEVER reach the DOM. null/missing = render nothing. Footnotes render ONCE in a single 'Notes & assumptions' section above the contact form. This is fleet financing only — equity/fundraise/counterparty content firewalls apply in full. Utilization-stack economics lead frame; upside rows are never summed into base totals; the tourism experience layer is the headline layer per the international addendum. All scenario figures transcribed exactly from the worked revenue model and re-verified by script before writing. Demand pools are sourced visitor/ridership flows, labeled indicative — no employer trackers exist on this run and no employer page exists (international addendum). No phasing or fleet-count section: no sourced Dubai fleet plan exists in the research set, so none renders.

fn1.text: Experience, charter and spot pricing is positioned against Dubai's operating water-leisure market: shared tours published at AED 65–425 per person, heritage abra hire at AED 300 per hour, and reported full-vessel ferry hire near AED 2,800 per hour.

fn2.text: Demand pool figures are indicative of demand potential along these corridors — sourced visitor and ridership flows, not commitments or commercial relationships.

fn3.text: Economics are indicative ranges with conservative defaults. Upside lines — sponsorship and overnight cargo — are never included in base totals.

fn4.text: All trip times respect Dubai's port, marina, creek and canal speed zones on a conservative planning basis. The maritime regulator sets authorised routes and speed limits route by route; a corridor-specific foil-borne allowance appears only as a separately labeled upside, never in base times.

fn5.text: Committed-seat pricing is a derived band, not a Dubai quote: anchored to published marine fares (AED 1–75), the water-taxi route band (AED 55–205), street-taxi plus road-toll costs, and premium ride-hail door-to-door for the same cross-city trip. Pending confirmation.

fn6.text: Crew costs use a UAE-adapted method: published UAE maritime wage surveys for a two-person crew (captain + deckhand), plus explicitly stated housing, transport, end-of-service, visa and medical allowances. The model uses $30 per hour loaded — the mid benchmark rounded up as a buffer.

fn7.text: Spot-seat lines are computed as fill rate × residual commute seat-legs × fare, with seats sold rounded down to whole seats; the stated seat count × fare is the exact revenue line.

fn8.text: The conservative case assumes deliberately thin fills and pays back in about 21 years — shown as the floor, not a financing case.

fn9.text: A 12-month operating year on warm, sheltered water. June–September heat shifts midday leisure sailings toward morning and evening slots; commuter peaks run unaffected in a climate-controlled cabin. Scenario counts are annual monthly averages with that shape absorbed.

fn10.text: Energy is priced at Dubai's published commercial electricity tariff with fuel surcharge and VAT — about $0.126 per kWh. At the program's standard $0.30 per kWh planning rate the energy line rises about 2.4×, and every scenario remains cash-positive.

fn11.text: All figures are US dollars. Local benchmarks are cited in UAE dirhams and convert at the pegged rate of 3.6725 dirhams per dollar.

fn12.text: The World Islands are partially developed today: the first operating resort is reported closed and other clusters are reported opening in phases. Island stops render as network reach, with no demand modeled on them.

copy.headline: Own the fleet behind Dubai's premium water network.
copy.subline: One vessel, four revenue layers. A tourism-weighted network on the Marina, the Water Canal, the Creek, the Palm and the Gulf shoreline that earns across the whole day — commuters, experiences, charters and spot seats — twelve months a year.
copy.small_print: Indicative economics — conservative defaults, ranges not points.

copy.headline: One asset. One day. Four demand layers.
copy.body: A commuter-only vessel earns in a fraction of its available hours — this network monetizes the whole day, twelve months a year. Committed seats form the schedule spine; tourism experiences and charters are the headline layer that carries the payback, priced against a water-leisure market Dubai already operates at scale.

opex_basis.crew: Per-scenario activity hours × $30/hr: 198/245/300 hrs = $5,940/$7,350/$9,000; rendered as the band.
opex_basis.energy: $1,108/$1,258/$1,435 per scenario; rendered as the band. Sensitivity at $0.30/kWh: line rises ~2.4× (+$1.5–2.0K/mo); nets stay positive in all scenarios (fn10).
opex_basis.maintenance: $82.5K/yr = $6,875/mo, program-consistent N45 figure, flat across scenarios.
opex_basis.berthing_insurance: $6,890/mo = berthing $2,723 (AED 10,000 assumption inside the sourced Dubai Marina band AED 6,000–30,000/mo, commercial terms TBD) + insurance $4,167 ($50K/yr placeholder ≈ 2% hull + P&I; UAE-licensed insurer mandatory).

navier_intro.title: Meet the vessel

copy.headline: A U.S.-built electric hydrofoil.
copy.body: Navier is a U.S. builder of electric hydrofoil vessels. Its N45 Explorer carries 30 passengers at a foilborne cruise speed of about 30 knots — lifted clear of the water for a smooth ride above the wake and wash of conventional hulls. The smaller N30 Quanta carries 8. Foiling cuts energy use by up to ~90% versus a conventional planing hull, and both vessels run near-silent on electric power.

tech_chips.label: Energy
tech_chips.value: up to ~90% less than a planing hull

copy.note: A vessel is a network asset, not stranded in one market — the multi-city network is the residual-value story.
